basic_information.short_title: Bangsamoro Sustainable Development Board Act of 2022
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT CREATING THE BANGSAMORO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT BOARD, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
basic_information.approved_by: Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim (signed; the date line on the signed copy is blank)
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after complete publication in a newspaper of general or regional circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates a joint national–regional board to set the region's sustainable development framework, and earmarks at least 1% of revenues from natural resource extraction in the Bangsamoro to run it — money protected from being deducted from the block grant.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To integrate economic, social and environmental considerations into how the region's natural resources are conserved, developed and used, under a framework the act grounds in both ecological and Islamic principles.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A board chaired by the Senior Minister and co-chaired by a national government official formulates the Bangsamoro Sustainable Development Framework, sets natural resource policy, and must review its own implementation every 5 years with Parliament taking part.
who_will_be_affected: Communities near natural resource extraction, whose revenues part-fund the Board
Women and marginalised groups, whose climate vulnerability the Board must address
Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples, whose rights the policy section recognises
NGOs, which elect one of their own onto the Board
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2022 — 15 days after complete publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. A joint national–regional board sets the region's sustainable development framework, funded by at least 1% of natural resource revenues — and that 1% cannot be clawed back out of the block grant.
in_practice: A Bangsamoro Sustainable Development Board chaired by the Senior Minister and co-chaired by a National Government official
Members include the environment, interior and finance ministers, the planning authority head, the Parliament's environment committee chair, and an NGO representative
The NGO representative is elected by recognised NGOs in a forum organised by the Bangsamoro Government, and sits as head of their organisation rather than personally
National Government representatives number no more than six
The Board formulates the Bangsamoro Sustainable Development Framework and natural resource policy
It must provide measures for environmental justice and for reducing the vulnerability of women and marginalised groups to climate change
It meets at least quarterly, with a simple majority as quorum
Not less than 1% of revenues from exploration, development and utilisation of natural resources in the region funds its operations
A mandatory review of the act's implementation 5 years in, and every 5 years after, with Parliament part of the process

for_specific_groups.Communities near mining, energy or other: At least 1% of the revenues collected from those activities is earmarked for the Board that sets the rules governing them.
for_specific_groups.Women and marginalised groups: Section 6(c) obliges the Board to provide measures reducing their vulnerability to climate change and variability.
for_specific_groups.Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples: The policy section recognises and promotes their rights within the framework of the Constitution and national laws.
for_specific_groups.NGOs: You elect one representative onto the Board from nominees submitted by recognised NGOs.
for_specific_groups.Settler communities, children and youth: All are named in the Social Justice and Well-Being principle of the Framework.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The whole BARMM, and natural resource activity within it.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Through the sustainable development framework and natural resource policies the Board adopts.
what_you_can_do: Ask for the Bangsamoro Sustainable Development Framework the Board is required to formulate and adopt
Ask about the mandatory five-year review, which Parliament must be part of
If you run a recognised NGO, take part in the forum that elects the NGO representative
watch_out_for: The Board sets frameworks and policies; it does not itself issue permits or enforce against polluters.
The signed copy carries the Chief Minister's signature above a blank date line.
Board members receive travel expenses and honoraria for every meeting attended, in amounts the Board itself fixes.
The 1% is of revenues collected — if little is collected, little is allocated.

key_terms_explained.Moral Governance: The act's governing principle — rules, practices and processes 'completely devoid of all the evils of graft and corruption', driven by dedication, devotion, honesty, justice and integrity.
key_terms_explained.Khalifa / Environmental Vicegerency: The Islamic concept of humankind as trustee and steward of the earth, used here as a principle of the development framework.
key_terms_explained.Block grant: The annual transfer from the National Government to the Bangsamoro under Section 21, Article XII of the Organic Law.
key_terms_explained.MENRE: Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy, which serves as the Board's regional secretariat.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Dhu Al-Qa'dah 24, 1443 / 23 June 2022. Signed by the Chief Minister; the date of approval is blank on the signed copy.

benefits.headline: A funded, joint board for sustainable development, with 1% of resource revenues ring-fenced for it.

direct_benefits.benefit: A comprehensive sustainable development framework for the region
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Formulated and adopted by the Board

direct_benefits.benefit: Dedicated funding from natural resource revenues, protected from block grant deduction
direct_benefits.amount: Not less than 1% of revenues from exploration, development and utilisation of natural resources in the region

direct_benefits.benefit: Measures on environmental justice and on women's and marginalised groups' climate vulnerability
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Required of the Board by Section 6(c)
Elected in a forum organised by the Bangsamoro Government

indirect_benefits: A standing forum where national and regional government sit together on resource policy
A mandatory five-yearly review that Parliament takes part in
limitations: The Board makes policy; it does not license or enforce.
The 1% depends on how much revenue is actually collected.
Honoraria and travel expenses are fixed by the Board itself.

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on the public.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy, which serves as the Board's secretariat
where_to_complain.oversight: The Bangsamoro Parliament, which is part of the mandatory five-year review, and its Committee on Environment, Natural Resources and Energy, whose chair sits on the Board
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A community near a mining operation asks what share of the revenue stays in the region's own environmental governance. At least 1% of what is collected from exploration, development and utilisation funds the Board — and it cannot be netted off against the block grant.

A women's organisation wants climate adaptation on the agenda. Section 6(c) requires the Board to provide measures reducing the vulnerability of women and marginalised groups to climate change and variability.
An NGO wants a say in resource policy. Recognised NGOs elect one representative onto the Board in a forum organised by the Bangsamoro Government.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: “The Bangsamoro Sustainable Development Board Act of 2022”.

Section 2 — Policies: protect and advance the right to a balanced and healthful ecology in accordance with the rhythm and harmony of nature; improve quality of life through careful planning taking account of ecological balance and the natural resources available to current and future generations; promote effective use of economic resources toward food security, economic development and social justice; provide equitable opportunities for constituent LGUs and strengthen governance systems for people's participation; ensure basic necessities and equal opportunities; recognise the role of women and youth and ensure their representation in decision-making and policy determining bodies; and recognise and promote the rights of Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples within the framework of the Constitution and national laws.

Section 3 — The Board formulates and adopts a Bangsamoro Sustainable Development Framework guided by the principle of Moral Governance — 'the set of rules, practices, and processes completely devoid of all the evils of graft and corruption, and explicitly driven by the moral principles of utmost dedication, devotion, honesty, justice, and integrity' — which serves as the compass and balancing power of four further principles: Environmental Vicegerency, invoking Khalifa, the trusteeship and stewardship of the earth; Social Justice and Well-Being, covering equity of access, basic services, housing, labour rights, and the rights and participation of women, youth, children and settler communities; Respect to Culture, Belief and Heritage across the region's ethno-linguistic groups; and Economic Progress with Equity.

Sections 4–5 — Creates the Bangsamoro Sustainable Development Board, composed of representatives of the National Government and the Bangsamoro Government, to ensure the integration and harmonisation of economic, social and environmental considerations. It is chaired by the Senior Minister and co-chaired by an appropriate National Government official, with the Ministers of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy, of the Interior and Local Government, and of Finance and Budget and Management; the Director-General of the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority; the Chair of the Parliament's Committee on Environment, Natural Resources and Energy; and an NGO representative elected from nominees submitted by recognised NGOs in a forum organised by the Bangsamoro Government, sitting as head of the organisation represented. National Government representatives shall not exceed six.

Section 6 — Powers: develop a comprehensive sustainable development framework ensuring proper conservation, development and utilisation of natural resources; formulate natural resource policies and plans; provide measures for environmental justice and governance and for reducing the vulnerability of women and marginalised groups to climate change and variability; promote effective and responsible use of economic resources toward growth, full employment, human development, gender equality and social justice; call on national agencies, LGUs or the private sector for opinions and advice; and monitor and review implementation of its policies and plans.

Sections 7–9 — Each government organises its own secretariat, the Bangsamoro Government's being the MENRE. The Board adopts its own internal rules, meets at least quarterly on prior notice to all members, does business on a simple majority quorum, and its members receive travel expenses and honoraria per meeting in amounts the Board fixes.

Section 10 — Initial funding is charged against the Contingent Fund of the 2022 General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro, with later years in the regular budget of the MENRE. An amount equivalent to not less than 1% of the revenues collected from the exploration, development and utilisation of any natural resources within the BARMM shall be allocated for the Board's operation, and that amount shall not be included in the amount deducted from the block grant under Section 21, Article XII of the Bangsamoro Organic Law. The National Government bears the expenses of its own secretariat and representation.

Section 11 — The Bangsamoro Government, through the Board, shall undertake a mandatory review of the act's implementation 5 years after implementation and every 5 years thereafter, with the Bangsamoro Parliament part of the process.
Section 14 — Takes effect 15 days after complete publication in a newspaper of general or regional circulation.

who_benefits: Communities affected by natural resource extraction
Women and marginalised groups facing climate vulnerability

citizen_questions.q: What does the Board actually do?
citizen_questions.a: It formulates the region's sustainable development framework and its policies for conserving, developing and using natural resources, provides measures for environmental justice and climate vulnerability, and monitors implementation. It does not issue permits or enforce against polluters.

Initially from the 2022 Contingent Fund, then the environment ministry's budget — plus at least 1% of revenues collected from exploration, development and utilisation of natural resources in the region.

citizen_questions.q: Why does it matter that the 1% is not deducted from the block grant?
citizen_questions.a: Without that clause the region could fund the Board out of resource revenues and then see the same amount netted off its annual block grant from the National Government — leaving it no better off. Section 10 expressly forbids that.
Yes. The Board is jointly composed, co-chaired by a National Government official, with up to six national representatives, and each government funds its own secretariat.

citizen_questions.q: Does civil society have a seat?
citizen_questions.a: Yes — one NGO representative, elected by recognised NGOs in a forum organised by the Bangsamoro Government, sitting as head of their organisation rather than in a personal capacity.
Section 11 requires a mandatory review of implementation 5 years in and every 5 years after, with Parliament part of the process.
